# Pinned skills

## commit-author v1.12.0

Write Conventional Commits messages from a staged diff. Activates only when the user explicitly asks to commit or write the message.

### Always-on rules
- Format: `<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>`.
- Types: feat (MINOR), fix (PATCH), refactor, perf, docs, style, test, build, ci, chore, revert.
- Subject: imperative mood (`add`, not `added`), max 50 characters, lowercase start, no trailing period.
- Body: explain why, not what; no line-by-line file summaries; hard wrap at 72 characters.
- Merge commits: keep the type/scope form; body summarizes all changes the merge brings in, grouped by type or area; footers reference the merged branch or PR.
- Revert: body references the reverted SHA.
- Footers: `BREAKING CHANGE:` followed by a migration path (forces a MAJOR bump); `Resolves #12`-style references at the bottom.

### Hard constraints
- Never include `Co-Authored-By: Claude` or any AI-attribution footer.
- Never volunteer a commit: no proposing commits at task end, no pre-staging, no `git add`/`git commit` as cleanup.
- Never run `git commit` without explicit go-ahead for the specific commit; each commit needs its own confirmation.
- When asked to draft a message, ask whether the user will commit or wants you to.
- Delegated commits are GPG signed if configured, unless the user opts out.

Invoke the full skill when: the user wants a commit message or asks to commit, and you need the merge-commit or breaking-change rules.

Full guide: invoke the commit-author skill.

## docs-architect v1.2.0

Purpose: one `docs/` tree where the folder is the doc type, frontmatter is the state, and moving a file is a state change.

### Always-on rules

- Pick the folder by the doc's job: `adr/` one decision; `ideas/` pre-plan; `plans/` scope and exit criteria; `designs/` how it is built; `reviews/` and `changes/` dated history; `guides/` and `methodology/` living `topic.md`; `backlog/`; `archive/` finished or obsolete.
- Scaffold: create `docs/README.md` and `docs/templates/`; create other folders when their first doc exists.
- Write-doc: copy the template, fill the frontmatter, link the doc to its origin.
- Frontmatter on every doc except `README.md`, `inbox.md`, `templates/`: `status`, `project`, `date`, `related`. ADRs use their own schema.
- Use relative markdown links; `related` paths are relative to `docs/`.
- Link ADRs from designs (`[ADR 0002](../adr/0002-slug.md)`) instead of restating reasoning.
- Write an ADR only for a real architecture decision (hard to reverse, surprising, real trade-off).
- ADR numbers: sequential; take the next by scanning `adr/`.
- Changing a decision: new ADR with `supersedes: N`; old one gets `status: superseded` and `superseded_by`.
- Backlog: queue layout (`inbox.md`, `<project>.md`, `done/YYYY-MM.md`) or item layout (`project.md`, `pending/`, `active/`, `done/`, `archive/`).
- Flow: inbox → ideas → plans → designs → adr → backlog. On close: item to `done/`, doc `status: done`, then `archive/`.
- Names: kebab-case, lowercase, no accents (`0004-use-nats.md`).
- Run the skill's `docs_lint.py [docs-dir]` (stdlib, read-only) before declaring a docs change done.

### Hard constraints

- Never edit an accepted ADR body; only `status` and `superseded_by`.
- Never rewrite reviews or changes; add a new dated doc.
- Never reuse an ADR number. Keep `adr/` flat; no per-project subfolder there.
- Create a per-project subfolder inside a type only after ~10 files of that type.
- Migrate: propose moves and renames, wait for approval, then move.
- Never duplicate these conventions in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`; point them at `docs/`.

Invoke the full skill when: setting up `docs/`, writing a plan/design/ADR/review, triaging a backlog, or reorganizing an existing docs folder.
Full guide: invoke the docs-architect skill.

## rsk-guide v0.5.1

Operator's summary of the `rsk` CLI: manage ralvaskills skills via the `.rsk/` manifest, bundles, global installs, and the `rsk mcp` server.

### Always-on rules

- Treat install, pin, update and uninstall as architectural decisions, not housekeeping.
- Before any state-changing action, state the action plainly: which skills or bundles, target scope (`--global` / `--for` / project manifest), and what changes on disk (including `.rsk/CLAUDE.md` and `./CLAUDE.md` when pinning).
- Quote the exact command, then wait for the user to confirm, redirect or decline.
- Use `--dry-run` when available if the user wants to preview.
- Confirm each bundle and each pin separately, even after a blanket "yes".
- Pin only skills that truly need auto-loading; installed-but-unpinned skills are not auto-loaded.
- Read-only commands (`rsk list`, `rsk catalog`, `rsk status` without `--stack`) need no confirmation.
- Verify flags against `rsk --help`; the CLI is still in progress (draft).

### Hard constraints

- Never run `rsk install`, `rsk uninstall`, `rsk update`, `rsk new`, `rsk destroy`, `rsk pin` or `rsk unpin` without explicit user confirmation.
- Ask first before `rsk status --stack` (network call). It is not yet implemented.
- Never promise drift checks until `--stack` ships.
- `rsk` must be on PATH for the `rsk mcp` server; `rsk new` skips MCP registration otherwise.

### MCP server (`rsk mcp`)

- Flow: `project_profile` (read-only) → propose to user → `install_skills` only after approval.
- Client forces approval on every `install_skills` call; this does not replace asking the user first.

Invoke the full rsk-guide skill for: setting up a project manifest or bundle, choosing pin vs install, global or official-cache installs, new-machine setup, the bundle list, `.rsk/` layout, or MCP server details.

Full guide: invoke the rsk-guide skill.

## token-economy v1.1.0

Spend tokens where they buy accuracy. Cut what persists (context, cache, always-loaded instructions) before what is said.

### Always-on rules
- Locate, then read: grep/glob or CodeGraph first; read line ranges; never re-read a file you just edited.
- Ask tools for the smallest useful answer: `git diff --stat` first, quiet flags, failing tests only, `tail`/`grep` on logs.
- Index web pages instead of reading them whole.
- Batch independent calls into one turn.
- Edit, don't rewrite; never print a file back.
- Ask before building on an ambiguous request.
- No pasted long output: run the command, or write to a file and read a range. Crop screenshots.
- Replies lead with the result; no recap, no narration.
- One task per session; carry it over in a handoff note, not the transcript.
- Two-failure rule: second failed attempt at the same thing, stop and escalate.
- Lookups of 1-3 tool calls stay inline; delegate only with a brief (goal, ruled out, where to look, output shape, word cap).
- Mechanical work (renames, checklist audits, repeated edits): script first, else cheap worker per batch. Verify with a command, not the worker's word.
- Default Sonnet at medium effort; escalate via subagent, then fresh session with handoff note. Switch model in place only while context is small.
- Effort: low for mechanical, medium default, high for real reasoning.
- Poll inside the 5-minute cache TTL or far beyond it, or let a script wait and report once.
- After a long break, `/clear` rather than resume a large context.
- Install only the skills and MCP servers a project uses.

### Hard constraints
- Never fork a deep context; brief a fresh subagent instead.
- Never use caveman style for commits, docs or code, nor user replies unless the user asked for caveman mode; it is for reports only a model reads.
- Never use opus or high effort on renames or mechanical edits.
- Ask before fixing: installs and edits to CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, settings.json, opencode.json(c), or agents.
- Don't quote a tool's savings percentage without measuring it here.

Full guide: invoke the token-economy skill.
